raw.details:
BuildAthon is an intensive 8-hour, one-day AI Hackathon hosted as part of Techvora '26 by the Department of Artificial Intelligence. Scheduled for November 24, 2026, at CAR LAB, BuildAthon challenges student teams to turn a real-world problem linked to the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) into a working AI prototype within a single day. Rather than training models from scratch, teams build practical solutions using pretrained models, free-tier APIs, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), prompting, and rule-based logic.

Guidelines & Eligibility

  • Who Can Participate: Open to all registered students with working programming or app-development knowledge. Prior model-training experience is not required.
  • Team Size & Composition:
  • Team Size: Strictly 3 members per team (no solo participation is allowed)
  • Team Matching: Students without a full team of 3 may contact the event coordinators before the registration deadline to be matched with other participants.
  • Participation Cap & Fee:
    • Up to 20 teams will be shortlisted across the problem statements.
    • Registration Fee: ₹750 per team (payable upon shortlisting confirmation).
    • Each participant may belong to only one team and must carry a valid student ID card on the event day.
  • Number of Problem Statements: 3 Problem Statements (teams select one; full problem statements are provided separately in the Problem Statements document).

Competition Process & Round Durations (8-Hour Event Schedule)

  1. Registration & Concept Note Submission (Deadline: November 23, 2026):
    • Teams submit member details, skill sets, chosen problem statement, an originality declaration, and a 1-page concept note (covering the problem, approach, tools/models, and SDG target).
    • Organizers shortlist up to 20 teams, notify them via email, and share sample datasets.
  2. Round 1 — PPT Pitch (Morning of November 24, 2026):
      • Duration: 5 minutes per team (3-minute pitch + 2-minute Q&A).
      • All 20 teams pitch across two rooms covering the problem, affected users, SDG link, architecture, tools/models, and responsible AI considerations.
      • Top 8 teams advance to Round 2 (announced before noon). Non-finalists attend a guest talk, feedback session, and vote for the People's Choice Award.
  3. Round 2 — Prototype Build & Live Demo (Afternoon of November 24, 2026):
    • Build Duration: 3 hours (ending at the 3:00 PM submission freeze). Organizers release 20–30 test inputs at the start of the build phase.
    • Demo Duration: 8 minutes per finalist team (5-minute live demo + 3-minute Q&A before the jury).
    • Results & Awards: Announced in the evening on the same day, concluding the 8-hour hackathon.

Rules & Regulations

  • Allowed Tools & APIs: Only open-source libraries, pretrained models, and free-tier APIs / free credits are allowed. Paid APIs are strictly prohibited.
  • Mandatory Disclosures: Teams must disclose all pretrained models, APIs, libraries, datasets, reused code, and AI coding assistants used during development.
  • Originality & Pre-Event Setup: Pre-event setup (creating accounts, generating API keys, and setting up an empty project skeleton) is permitted if disclosed, but the core solution must be built on the event day (GitHub commit history may be audited). Presenting an existing complete project as new is prohibited.
  • Feature Transparency: Teams must clearly distinguish working features from simulated or planned features during their demo.
  • Data Privacy & Ethics: Only public, synthetic, or anonymized data may be used. Entering private or sensitive personal data into any AI tool is forbidden. Solutions must address responsible AI practices, including handling wrong, uncertain, or harmful outputs.
  • Mentor & Conduct Guidelines: Mentors may guide and clarify doubts but cannot write code, design solutions, or operate demos. Sharing code or ideas with competing teams during the event is prohibited.
  • Submission Freeze & Hardware: All Round 2 deliverables (working prototype, backup demo video, GitHub link with README, test input outputs, final PPT, and SDG/Responsible AI notes) must be submitted before 3:00 PM; late submissions are not accepted. Teams must bring their own laptops and chargers (Wi-Fi, power, and backup hotspots are provided).
  • Disqualification: Plagiarism, falsifying results, using paid APIs, undisclosed external help/code, misrepresenting simulated features as working, data privacy violations, system attacks, or missing deadlines will lead to immediate disqualification. The decisions of the organizers and judges are final.

Judging Criteria (100 Marks Total)

  • Round 1 — PPT Pitch (30 Marks): Problem Understanding & SDG Relevance (10), Approach & Architecture (10), Innovation (5), Pitch Clarity (5).
  • Round 2 — Prototype Demo (70 Marks): Technical Implementation & AI Integration (20), Working Prototype (15), Output Quality on Organizer Test Inputs (10), Responsible AI & Privacy (10), Innovation & Scalability (5), UI/UX (5), Q&A & Teamwork (5).

Awards & Contact

  • Awards: 1st Place, 2nd Place, 3rd Place, People's Choice Award (audience vote), and Participation Certificates for all attendees.
  • Event Coordinators:
    • Sanjeev Pranay D: 9063316027
    • Mohana S: 8122640389
    • Email: sanjeevpranays@gmail.com

teams must pay the registration fee of ₹750 per team via UPI to 9063316027 (Sanjeev Pranay D) to confirm their participation. (Please share the payment screenshot/transaction ID to the same number, with the coordinator upon completing the transfer.)
